$comment: Participant TCT claims-sibling convention as in bundle-001 (tct_claims next to each __JWS_TCT__; minter strips the companions before signing the bundle with __VALID_A_SIG__). The `extensions` member is an ordinary member of the signed inner body, so it is covered by the JCS-canonical signing input like any other member (RFC-AITP-0010 §3 field table; RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4.1) — coverage comes from `extensions` being a body member other than `signature` itself, not from its textual position in this JSON: JCS (RFC 8785) sorts object members lexicographically before hashing, so the pre-canonicalization ordering shown here has no bearing on what the signature covers. Uses the `extensions.tee` container reserved by RFC-AITP-0012 §3 ("Any AITP payload MAY carry an `extensions` object"), so the key is registered rather than invented.
description: Session Trust Bundle carrying an OPTIONAL `extensions` member on the inner body (RFC-AITP-0010 §3 field table; RFC-AITP-0012). Otherwise identical to bundle-001 — coordinator signature, both embedded TCT compact JWS strings, expiry window, and version checks all pass. The bundle's `extensions.tee` object uses the Trusted Execution Environment container reserved (non-normative for v0.2) by RFC-AITP-0012 §3: unknown keys inside `extensions` MUST be ignored and MUST NOT drive a trust decision, but the member itself is a schema-permitted, ordinary part of the signed body. The receiving participant (B in this fixture) accepts the bundle: `extensions` is present, well-formed, and does not affect any of the RFC-AITP-0010 §5 verification steps. Coordinator key source: `input.coordinator_manifest` carries the coordinator's (kat-keypair-001) signed Manifest; the bundle signature and the embedded TCTs verify under the key it designates (RFC-AITP-0010 §5 step 5).

expected.rationale: Bundle signature verifies under the coordinator's key over the JCS-canonical inner body INCLUDING the `extensions` member (excluded only: `signature` itself); both embedded TCT compact JWS strings verify; receiver's AID is in participants; expires_at = min of the embedded TCTs' exp claims. The unknown-to-core `extensions.tee` object does not affect the outcome: it is ignored for trust-decision purposes per RFC-AITP-0001 §7 and RFC-AITP-0012 §5, but remains part of the signed bytes and MUST NOT be treated as an unpermitted field.
